body.statement: For sample sizes in the deterministic eventual regime \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal M}T_n(P)\ge T_0\), uniformly over observed laws \(P\in\mathcal M\), \(\widehat{\mathcal V}_n/\mathcal V(P)\to1\) and \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal M}\Pr_P(\widehat T_n\ge T_0)\to1\). On \(\{\widehat T_n\ge T_0\}\), \(b(\widehat T_n)-b(T_n(P))=o_P(a(T_n(P)))\) and \(a(\widehat T_n)/a(T_n(P))\to1\). Hence the eventual-regime analytic critical value \(\widehat q_{n,\alpha}\), built from the exact Palm-intensity expansion, and the canonical-simulation critical value \(\widehat q^{\mathrm{sim}}_{n,\alpha}\), built from \(n^2\) copies of the prescribed padded grid target, satisfy \(\Pr_P\{S_n(\theta)\le\widehat q_{n,\alpha}\}\to1-\alpha\) and \(\Pr_P\{S_n(\theta)\le\widehat q^{\mathrm{sim}}_{n,\alpha}\}\to1-\alpha\), uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal M\); both critical values equal \(+\infty\) on the vanishing complement \(\{\widehat T_n<T_0\}\).
body.justification: Pointwise pivotality does not remove the population-dependent number of effective LR opportunities, so the spatial clock must be estimated at the centering scale.
body.gap: Takatsu and Westling (2025) estimate ingredients for Gaussian uniform bands, and Westling, Gilbert, and Carone (2020) study a pointwise isotonic scale; neither propagates a plug-in LR clock through Gumbel centering.
body.consumer: It turns the canonical law into a usable critical value without estimating tiny single-location tail probabilities from the observational data.

obligation.what_is_open: Calibration remains conditional on the unresolved canonical and causal-transfer limits, including random-horizon uniformity and padded-grid quantile approximation.
obligation.obstruction: Relative clock consistency controls centering and scale substitution but cannot create the missing Gumbel law or show that the finite padded simulation target and continuum maximum have asymptotically identical quantiles.
obligation.attempted: The uniform positive lower bound for the spatial volume, inverse-centering mean-value expansion, scale substitution, and conditional empirical-distribution error for the prescribed number of simulations were derived.
obligation.partial_result:
The frozen lower bounds imply
\[
 \mathcal V(P)
 \ge |J|\left\{\frac{c_g c_\theta^2}{4V_\kappa}\right\}^{1/3}>0,
\]
because \(f(a)=\int g(a\mid w)p(w)\,dw\ge c_g\int p(w)\,dw=c_g\).  Thus \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal M}T_n(P)\to\infty\).  If the unresolved uniform plug-in result supplies \(\widehat{\mathcal V}_n/\mathcal V(P)=1+o_P(1)\), then
\[
 \log\frac{\widehat T_n}{T_n(P)}=o_P(1)
\]
and \(\Pr_P(\widehat T_n\ge T_0)\to1\) uniformly.  On that event, the mean-value theorem applied to \(\mathcal E_\star(b(T))=\log T\) gives
\[
 \frac{b(\widehat T_n)-b(T_n(P))}{a(T_n(P))}
 =\frac{\mathcal E_\star'(b(T_n(P)))}{\mathcal E_\star'(\widetilde b_n)}
   \log\frac{\widehat T_n}{T_n(P)}=o_P(1),
\]
where \(\widetilde b_n\) lies between the two centerings.  Since \(\mathcal E_\star'(u)=\beta_\star+\gamma_\star/u\) and both centerings diverge,
\[
 \frac{a(\widehat T_n)}{a(T_n(P))}
 =\frac{\mathcal E_\star'(b(T_n(P)))}
        {\mathcal E_\star'(b(\widehat T_n))}
 \longrightarrow1.
\]
Therefore Slutsky's theorem would transfer an established canonical Gumbel law to the analytic feasible critical value.  For the simulation route, conditionally on the data, the Dvoretzky--Kiefer--Wolfowitz inequality for \(n^2\) independent simulated maxima gives an empirical-distribution error \(O_P(n^{-1})\).  Quantile consistency still requires the unresolved padded-grid approximation, random-horizon uniformity, and anti-concentration or strict limiting-distribution continuity.  The clock calculus cannot create those upstream facts.
